_why: THE TABLES tools/gennpcdrops.py CANNOT READ OUT OF THE SCRIPTS, and why each one is here.
The generator runs every [ai_queue3] death trigger through its own small RuneScript
interpreter, which is the whole point of it: a drop table is script, not data, and a hand-kept
copy would be wrong the first time anybody edited a table. What it follows is the trigger, the
labels it jumps to and the procs it calls. What it does NOT follow is a drop handed to the
killer through queue() - the trigger ends, the reward runs later on the player - and it cannot
answer a varp, so a drop whose identity comes out of one is not a thing it can work out either.
A row in here is therefore a drop the viewer should show that the interpreter has no way to
reach, written out by hand with the reason. It is not a place to put a table that is merely
inconvenient to derive: if the generator can reach it, it must, and gennpcdrops exits with an
error if an npc named here turns out to be derivable after all, so this file cannot quietly

why: The behemoth's spice is not dropped at all: [ai_queue3,hundred_dave_hellrat_behemoth]
queues hundred_dave_behemoth_reward onto the hero, and THAT hands over the shaker - which
is deliberate and the script says why (a proc writing a player varp has its
p_active_player requirement credited to the call site, and inside an ai_queue nothing has
been found yet). So there is no obj_add in the trigger for the interpreter to see.
And the colour is %hundred_dave_behemoth_colour, written when the player pulls the curtain
back, so WHICH shaker you get is not rolled - it is the curtain's. Every kill gives exactly
one 4-dose shaker of one of four colours, which is why the four rows are 1/4 each: it is
the only honest thing a per-item viewer can say about 'one of these four, always'. Four
rows of 'Always' would read as four shakers a kill.
These four rows are what the file carried from the day the viewer was built (3780c83c) and
they are unchanged here; what is new is that re-running the generator keeps them instead of
dropping them, which is what gamemode_battery's gennpcdrops --check had been failing on.
